name: Monday Madness

date.source: TEST/monday%20card.htm's own headline, "FOR 12 JUNE 2000", served as /promotions/ufw-ultra-2000/archive/ufw-monday-madness-card-jun12-2000.html

notes: Billed only. The federation's own advance card, headlined "FOR 12 JUNE 2000", from an earlier copy of its Monday card page. No results for this night survive. The card bills eleven matches, four of them for titles, and the Titleholder History dates two title changes to this night: the Rising Star title to Havok and the TV title to JiN.

name: Battle of the Titans

date.source: The federation's own front page (/promotions/ufw-ultra-2000/archive/ufw-front-page.html), its PPV Archive list: "Battle of the Titans 2000 (26 March 2000)".

evidence.note: Its PPV Archive list names and dates the PPV: "Battle of the Titans 2000 (26 March 2000)".
Captured as its outer frame only: both content frames, under /cgi-bin/framed/, sat behind the host's robots.txt and were never captured.

Eight title changes dated 2000-03-26: World (Insomniac to Mike Nightmare), US (Layeth the Smack Down to The Total Package), Tag Team (The Avator & Biohazard to The Natural Disasters), Cruiserweight (Ice to Jaguar), Woman's (Fury to Pandora), TV (Iceman to Kaos), Hardcore (Cain Manson Crow to Jake "Showtime" Douglas), and the Rising Star Title's inaugural reign (The Gimp).

notes: The PPV's results page survives only as its outer frame; the frames that carried the results were never captured. Eight titles changed hands on the night, per the federation's own Titleholder History.

name: Ring Rage

date.source: The federation's own front page (/promotions/ufw-ultra-2000/archive/ufw-front-page.html), its PPV Archive list: "Ring Rage 2000 (30 April 2000)"; its retrospective of Roody Poo agrees: "at Ring Rage 2000 (Sunday, April 30, 2000)".

evidence.note: Its PPV Archive list names and dates the PPV: "Ring Rage 2000 (30 April 2000)".
Captured as its outer frame only: both content frames, under /cgi-bin/framed/, sat behind the host's robots.txt and were never captured.
The federation's own retrospective dates Ring Rage 2000 to Sunday, 30 April 2000, and quotes Roody Poo's statement that night: left off the card days after his World Title reign (24–26 April 2000).

Seven title changes dated 2000-04-30: World (Mike Nightmare to Iceman), US (The Total Package to Myst), Tag Team (Iceman & Myst to The Avator & Biohazard), Woman's (Pandora to Fury), TV (Iceman to Howler), Hardcore (Ed to The Gimp), and the Stables Title ("???" to The Legion).

notes: The PPV's results page survives only as its outer frame; the frames that carried the results were never captured. Seven titles changed hands on the night, per the federation's own Titleholder History, and Roody Poo's statement that night complains that he was left off the card.

name: Roody Poo Night

date.source: The federation's own retrospective of Roody Poo tells of the Night before his World Title reign (24–26 April 2000) and gives it no date; the front page's PPV Archive lists "Roody Poo Night Results" undated.

evidence.note: Its PPV Archive list carries "Roody Poo Night Results", undated.
Captured as its outer frame only: both content frames, under /cgi-bin/framed/, sat behind the host's robots.txt and were never captured.

The federation's own account: "UFW decides to reward the master of the Poo Bomb... for months of tireless service... by holding Roody Poo Night. Many jobs done by Roody Poo in the past were reciprocated on this day by grateful UFW roster members, most notably top 10 star and future Heavyweight Champion, Insomniac!" and "Roody Poo night comes and goes, with Roody Poo compiling a massive 11 wins, 35 losses, including one to Bob the Chair (Ed's \"valet\")."

notes: No card or results for the night survives; its results page is only an outer frame. The federation's own retrospective tells of it: roster members repaid Roody Poo's many losses that day, "most notably top 10 star and future Heavyweight Champion, Insomniac!"

name: Live in London 2000

date.source: The event's own Info page: "-Date :The 20th of August 2000"; the Card page repeats it: "20th of August 2000".

matches.note: Billed on the card as "BATTLE ROYAL {Includes Everyone in the UFW, Winner Goes to Match 12}" and staged in the results as a "47 Man... Over The Top Battle Royal". Only the entrants the results name are listed. The pre-show Info page said Mimic and Mike Nightmare could not attend because of travel difficulty; the results have Mimic in this match.

matches.title: ufw-ultra-2000-rising-star
matches.note: Billed on the card as "TOURNEY... RISING STAR TITLE" against Chasm; the results text stages it as a standard title defense ("still UFW Rising Star champion, 'The Scholar' Howard Porter").

matches.title: ufw-ultra-2000-rising-star
matches.note: A second, unbilled Rising Star defense the same night: the card names only one Rising Star challenger (Chasm, match above), but the results text stages this separate Ladder Match against Ming, again won by Porter ("still UFW Rising Star champion"). Nick Taylor ran in with a baseball bat afterward.

matches.title: ufw-ultra-2000-cruiserweight
matches.note: Billed as "MATCH 10 - CRUISERWEIGHT TITLE (Gimmick TBA), Mayhem vs Professor Herbert D. Dorkiman"; the results declare "new UFW Cruiserweight champion".

matches.title: ufw-ultra-2000-tv
matches.note: Billed as "MATCH 14 - TV TITLE (Gimmick TBA), Mayhem vs B.A. Bruiser", cross-checked against the Titleholder History page's own change of TV champion to B.A. Bruiser dated 2000-08-20.

matches.title: ufw-ultra-2000-hardcore
matches.note: Billed as "MATCH 13 - HARDCORE TITLE (Gimmick TBA), The Body vs Hex"; the results declare "new UFW Hardcore champion".

matches.title: ufw-ultra-2000-us
matches.note: Billed as "MATCH 15 - US TITLE (Gimmick TBA), Anguish vs 'The Scholar' Howard Porter"; the results declare "new UFW US champion", and the Titleholder History dates Porter's US title to 2000-08-20.

matches.title: ufw-ultra-2000-world
matches.note: The main event, billed as "UFW WORLD TITLE (Gimmick TBA), Kaos (c) vs Myst vs Mayhem"; the Titleholder History dates Myst's World title to 2000-08-20.

evidence.note: The event's own news/preview page: date, venue, run-by, and the Buckingham Palace tournament-venue detail.
The event's own advertised card: 15 numbered matches plus a 7-match Special Event Title tourney bracket.
The tourney bracket's own results text (rounds one through three).
Results text, part three: the Cruiserweight Title match and the Emerald Fusion/Biohazard segment.
Results text, part four: the Hardcore, US and World Title matches.

notes: Staged at Earls Court, London, per the event's own Info page, with the tournament bracket staged at Buckingham Palace ("driven to Buckingham Palace to take part in their matches"). The seven tournament-bracket matches and the special-event segments are in the served results pages and are not listed below.

matches.note: Billed referee Revenant abandoned the match to attack Biohazard's tag partner Revenant was feuding with; Bill Fraser stepped in as replacement referee (served page narrates it in full).

No winner declared. Howard Porter turned on his own partner mid-match and joined Dorkiman and Taylor in beating him down; the referee called for the bell rather than ruling a finish (served page narrates the turn in full).
No winner declared. The match was interrupted by an angle in which Mayhem and Anguish allied against the Forsaken Brotherhood; the served page never resolves a finish.
